sections.title: Alpine rose
sections.text: A deciduous shrub native from Europe east to Kazakhstan. Its upright or slightly arching stems are about 1–2 m tall; it is usually less prickly than many roses. Single or few pink to rose-red flowers are about 4–6 cm across. The elongated red hips hang downward and often lose their sepals at maturity.

sections.title: Comparison and use
sections.text: The solitary bright-pink flower and narrow pendant hip in the plate are characteristic of this rose. A Bulgarian flora describes its fruits as useful to the food industry, but the sources do not establish a specific household preparation or toxicity assessment.
